items.title: Courtney O'Neill, Centre Wellington Community Foundation
notes: Re: Smart Cities Report

C. O’Neill, Nutritious Food Coordinator outlined her role to increasing community food access, with a focus on bringing multi-sector stakeholders together to shape how our community can best respond to the increased food needs through knowledge sharing, collective learning and system thinking. She explained household food insecurity, indicating 24% of Ontario households experienced food insecurity in 2023 and 30% of children lived in a food-insecure household in Ontario in 2023.

C. O’Neill outlined the community impact various programs such as summer student nutrition support, community food outreach program, free safe food handler certification and multi-partner projects and resource sharing have on the community. She outlined the next steps to increased food access are to secure funding, measure the impact and establish new pathways for distribution and program delivery.
C. O’Neill responded to questions regarding healthy food vending machines and innovative ways to distribute healthy and affordable food.

items.title: County Council Report - Councillor Mary Lloyd, County Ward 5
notes: Councillor Mary Lloyd provided highlights of the OPP annual report, Housing services and activity report, mental health training in the daycare centres, the volunteer appreciation video, and the various ongoing activities at the museum. She outlined ongoing activities at the various library branches, shared comments submitted by the County regarding Bill 185, informed Council of a public meeting regarding the reallocation of employment lands upcoming in June and spoke about the increase to the cost of garbage bags and waste diversion measures.
Councillor MacDonald asked if a representative of the Police Services Board would provide an update to Council.

items.title: Pierre Chauvin, MHBC Planning re: item 8.1 - Official Plan and Zoning
notes: Amendment (OP02/23 and RZ05/23) - Status Update, 19/19A East Mill Street, Elora
P. Chauvin indicated the revised design now proposes a 4-storey mixed use building, extending along the East Mill Street frontage. He highlighted the details of Building A, including:
• 3 ground floor commercial units (252m²)
• 18 accessible dwelling units
• 22 residential parking spaces provided in a basement parking garage • 4-storey building height (14.5m) in order to maintain 18 units above flood elevation
and the Building B to the rear of the property:
• 2 storey stone building will be converted from a casket manufacturing facility to a restaurant and/or retail
• Addition is proposed along with outdoor patio area
• 11 outdoor parking spaces to serve all commercial use on the property, including buildings A and B

P, Chauvin Design highlighted the design changes and rationale, presented various artist renderings and noted the heritage mitigation & conservation efforts. He responded to questions of clarification.

items.title: Rich Wigmore & Jason Castellan, Elora Rocks Hockey Club
notes: re: item 8.2 Elora Rocks Agreement

Rich Wigmore & Jason Castellan provided an update regarding the ongoing action of the Hockey Club, including reinstatement of a Board of Directors, a petition of support with over 250 signatures from the community, stronger relationship with staff in Parks & Recreation, and not-for profit status in good standing.

Jason Castellan, Chairman of the Board and former Rocks Player, indicated after working with staff they have a good understanding of the terms of the deferral agreement and introduced a slight change asking that the remittance of the payment be at the end of the season rather than at the beginning. He noted management is trying to reorganize and seek corporate sponsorship in order to meet the payment schedule.

items.title: John Scott, Gentre Wellington Greenlanes re Agenda Item 8.7 -
notes: Decision Report - South Fergus Secondary Plan (OPA 14)

John Scott noted his support for Council’s direction to set the height limit at 6 storeys over 8 storeys in the Secondary Plan and suggested looking at Europe for development trends related to density. He suggested defining what liveability looks like and providing secured bike storage in multi unit developments as well as safe passage over or under Highway 6.
